about: Model-provider lane falsifiers: each selftest entry breaks one falsify.py check, MP01 plants a wrapping add in counted_input_tokens so an overflowing repeated prefix no longer refuses, MP02-MP04 break the 60-second idle release behaviour, MP05-MP10 weaken the context-window admission tests, MP11 plants a nonzero cache size in the launched engine arguments, MP12-MP14 misreport the journal write outcome (a denied write as corrupt, a non-permission write as denied, and a denial without its operation), and MP15-MP16 bypass the shared journal write mapper at the replace and write call sites. The `did` and `wallet` commands share one provider-crate table with `provider`; PV43 maps `did` to the wallet manifest, PV44 and PV45 drop a did or wallet recovery target from PROVIDER_TARGETS, PV46 bypasses the refusal of an edit whose file does not exist, and PV47 and PV48 drop the model or the did confinement test harness target so a killed run leaves a mutated harness behind, and PV49 drops wallet's falsifier honesty test target, which wallet's list mutates (WP25). PV50 maps `capsule-identity` to the wasm-capsule manifest, and PV51-PV53 drop capsule-identity's source, test support or fixture target from PROVIDER_TARGETS, which the lab's list mutates. PV54 and PV55 remove or over-extend the failed test's own captured section that keeps a quoted child standard error out of the harness error search, and PV56-PV59 accept the end of the output as its closing delimiter, match the section header anywhere on a line, end the section at its last delimiter, remove only the first section, and PV60 lets a line that starts with the closing delimiter and goes on close a section. PV61-PV64 read the loader or Cargo marker after the section removal, accept text after the section header, and close a section at a line that ends with the closing delimiter. MP17-MP20 break the post-reap group probe for a zombie-only group on the Mac: MP17 restores the immediate EPERM failure, MP18 makes an EPERM that lasts to the deadline a bare timeout, MP19 accepts that EPERM as closure without ESRCH, and MP20 drops the deadline's closure reason; their evidence is macOS only. Files are relative to examples/agent-host. PV75-PV84 drop one of the wasm lab's ten edit and run-log recovery targets, so a killed lab run leaves that file mutated. PV85-PV95 break the unmutated baseline: the run proves each named test passes without the edit before it credits the edit, and these entries skip, accept, reorder or bypass that proof. PV96-PV101 break the edit-path refusal, so an absolute path, a climb out or an outside symlink cannot mutate a file: the whole refusal, the absolute guard, the containment base, symlink resolution, the check order and the pre-edit pass. PV102-PV103 remove the shared check of the mutation parent or temporary write target, so an outside parent that links back inside and an outside temporary symlink are refused before any link, write or replacement. PV104 drops the exclusive temporary create, so an existing hard link sends the write outside the repository, and PV105 leaves the backup name after a restore that replaced nothing. PV106 and PV107 remove ownership on replacement, so competing runs lose their newly acquired backup or temporary file; the cases exercise both names and the second mutation restores its original.

falsifiers.title: the temporary file is not created exclusively, so an existing hard link sends the write outside

edits.old:
tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".falsify-tmp")
                # The temporary file is this run's own destination: create it
                # exclusively, so a path that already exists (including a hard
                # link to a file outside REPO) is a refusal with its reason
                # instead of a truncating write into that file's inode.
                try:
                    handle = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o666)
                except FileExistsError as error:
                    raise BackupCollision(
                        f"{tmp} is a temporary file this run did not create; "
                        "the edit is not applied") from error
                tmp_owned = True
                try:
                    with os.fdopen(handle, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
                        stream.write(text)
                    saved = block_interruptions()
                    try:
                        replace_owned_file(tmp, path)
                        tmp_owned = False
                    finally:
                        restore_interruptions(saved)
                finally:
                    if tmp_owned and tmp.exists():
                        tmp.unlink()
edits.new:
tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".falsify-tmp")
                try:
                    tmp.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
                    os.replace(tmp, path)
                finally:
                    if tmp.exists():
                        tmp.unlink()
